# 🗂️ Reader-Document Disposition Ledger: `ose-public`

The single accountable record of what this program does to every tracked Markdown file in
`ose-public`, and why. No file in scope may be absent from it, no file may carry two terminal
dispositions, and no `follow-up-required` state may survive to archival.

This document quotes **no document body**, no command output, no configuration value, and no
credential. It records paths, classifications, commands, and verdicts only.

## Recorded Revision

| Field                     | Value                                                 |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Repository                | `ose-public`                                          |
| Recorded `origin/main`    | `028e8eed9e68112c49ccdee92d3cf29e70e6a4da`            |
| Enumeration command       | `git ls-tree -r --name-only <sha> \| grep -E '\.md$'` |
| Independent cross-check   | `git diff --name-only <empty-tree> <sha> -- '*.md'`   |
| Tracked Markdown files    | 9,294                                                 |
| Tracked `README.md` files | 1,004                                                 |

The enumeration reads a recorded commit rather than the working tree, so another actor's staged
changes cannot contaminate the inventory. It filters with `grep` rather than a `-- '*.md'` pathspec
because `git ls-tree` does not support glob pathspec magic and the pathspec form returns an empty
list without erroring.

## Disposition Vocabulary

Every path resolves to exactly one of these. The first eight are terminal; `follow-up-required` is
explicitly non-terminal and blocks archival.

| Disposition          | Terminal | Meaning                                                                                                               |
| -------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rewrite`            | yes      | The document's purpose or structure no longer serves its reader.                                                      |
| `targeted-fix`       | yes      | A bounded factual, command, link, tone, or navigation defect requires an edit.                                        |
| `link-only`          | yes      | The document stays short and routes detail to a canonical source.                                                     |
| `verified-unchanged` | yes      | It already meets the reader, fact, link, and voice checks.                                                            |
| `generated`          | yes      | A canonical source owns it; regenerate and validate instead of hand-editing.                                          |
| `historical-exempt`  | yes      | It records completed or archived work and stays untouched.                                                            |
| `identity-bound`     | yes      | Inside this plan's no-edit scope for `rhino-cli`; audit only. Most, not all, are byte-identical — see § Safety Gates. |
| `not-reader-doc`     | yes      | Inventoried, but not living repository-facing documentation.                                                          |
| `follow-up-required` | **no**   | Needs a separately scoped change before this plan can close. Blocks archival.                                         |

### Interim Classification Labels

Two further values appear in the `Disposition` column of the per-document rows before execution
touches them. They are **not** members of the terminal vocabulary above — they are the
classification-rule labels assigned at inventory time, and every one of them is replaced by a
terminal value when its row executes.

| Label            | Meaning                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `audit-required` | The document is in scope and must be audited; the audit decides the terminal disposition.     |
| `reader-related` | The document is in scope through a named defect or fact claim; its row states the exact edit. |

A row still holding `audit-required` or `reader-related` after its owning task is `Done` is a
defect, and P7-001 fails on it. Zero rows may carry an interim label at archival.

## Classification Rules

Ordered, first match wins, evaluated against the repository-relative path. Every rule is a
mechanical predicate so the classification is reproducible rather than remembered.

| #   | Path predicate                                                  | Disposition         | Reason                                                                                                                                      |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | any `README.md`                                                 | `audit-required`    | A README is a directory's entry point, so every one is audited and given an explicit disposition before any exemption is applied in P1-003. |
| 2   | `apps/rhino-cli/**` or `specs/apps/rhino/behavior/rhino-cli/**` | `identity-bound`    | This plan edits nothing under either path. The byte-identity boundary is the narrower subset below; the rest is out of scope by plan rule.  |
| 3   | `plans/done/**` or `archived/**`                                | `historical-exempt` | Records completed or archived work; historical claims are not rewritten to match the present.                                               |
| 4   | `.agents/**` or `.opencode/**`                                  | `generated`         | An auto-generated harness mirror. Regenerate from its canonical `.claude/` source; never hand-edit.                                         |
| 5   | `generated-reports/**`                                          | `not-reader-doc`    | Build output swept at any time; not living documentation.                                                                                   |
| 6   | `apps/*/content/**`                                             | `not-reader-doc`    | Educational and marketing content owned by its own app, not repository onboarding.                                                          |
| 7   | `social-media-posts/**`                                         | `not-reader-doc`    | Published post copy, not repository-facing documentation.                                                                                   |
| 8   | `docs/**` or a root-level `*.md`                                | `reader-related`    | The reader-facing documentation tree plus the repository's top-level entry points — the heart of this program's scope.                      |
| 9   | `specs/**`                                                      | `not-reader-doc`    | Specification and Gherkin bodies. Behaviour truth, consumed by tests rather than read as onboarding.                                        |
| 10  | `plans/**` (live)                                               | `not-reader-doc`    | Live plan bodies. They expire by design and are not a durable reader surface.                                                               |
| 11  | `repo-governance/**`                                            | `not-reader-doc`    | Normative convention bodies. Binding on contributors but not a newcomer reader journey; their README indexes are audited under rule 1.      |
| 12  | `.claude/**`                                                    | `not-reader-doc`    | Agent and skill definitions. Harness configuration rather than reader documentation; their README catalogs are audited under rule 1.        |
| 13  | everything else                                                 | `reader-related`    | Any remaining living document under an application, library, or infrastructure tree.                                                        |

## Exemption Overrides

Rule 1 is evaluated first so every one of the 1,004 READMEs is audited and carries an explicit
disposition. Auditing 373 of them then reaches an exempt verdict: they sit under a tree this plan
must not hand-edit. Those overrides are applied here, after the audit, not by skipping it.

| Exempt tree                                                   | Final disposition   | Paths     | Of which README | Why the plan does not hand-edit it                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | --------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apps/rhino-cli/**`, `specs/apps/rhino/behavior/rhino-cli/**` | `identity-bound`    | 27        | 20              | No-edit scope. 25 of the 27 are byte-identical with the private sibling; the other 2 are excluded by plan rule. |
| `plans/done/**`, `archived/**`                                | `historical-exempt` | 1,390     | 236             | Completed and archived work. Historical claims are not rewritten to match the present.                          |
| `.agents/**`, `.opencode/**`                                  | `generated`         | 649       | 117             | Harness mirrors. Regenerate from the canonical `.claude/` source; a hand-edit is drift.                         |
| **Total**                                                     | —                   | **2,066** | **373**         | None is scheduled for hand-editing.                                                                             |

Effective dispositions after the overrides, which must still total the tracked corpus:

| Disposition                         | Paths     |
| ----------------------------------- | --------- |
| `audit-required` (READMEs in scope) | 631       |
| `reader-related`                    | 183       |
| `not-reader-doc`                    | 6,414     |
| `historical-exempt`                 | 1,390     |
| `generated`                         | 649       |
| `identity-bound`                    | 27        |
| **Total**                           | **9,294** |

no edit row and is recorded as `verified-unchanged` instead of being rewritten into work.

No edit row.                                                                                                       |

## Per-Document Row Schema

Every audit-required or reader-related document receives one row carrying all seventeen fields
below. The bulk classes — historical, generated, identity-bound, and `not-reader-doc` — are carried
by their classification rule and matched count rather than by one literal row each; P1-007 proves
that split covers the tree exactly, with no path counted twice and none missed.

| Field                    | Meaning                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Repository revision      | The recorded `origin/main` SHA the row was derived from.                                                |
| Document kind            | `readme`, `tutorial`, `how-to`, `reference`, `explanation`, `governance`, `spec`, `plan`, `other`.      |
| Exact path               | Repository-relative, byte-exact.                                                                        |
| Audience                 | Which persona the document serves: product person, early-level engineer, returning maintainer, or none. |
| Purpose                  | One line on what the reader should be able to do after reading it.                                      |
| Disposition              | An interim classification label before execution, one terminal vocabulary value after.                  |
| Owning unit              | The delivery unit that executes the row: contract, refresh, fixes, or closeout.                         |
| Task ID                  | The delivery checklist ID that owns the row.                                                            |
| Direct action            | The one concrete edit or check to perform — never "update related docs".                                |
| Source of truth          | The authority the row's facts are resolved from.                                                        |
| Exact applicable command | The command that proves the row, or `None` for a pure editorial row.                                    |
| Acceptance criterion     | The concrete, falsifiable condition that closes the row.                                                |
| Date                     | Execution date.                                                                                         |
| Status                   | `Pending`, `Done`, or `Blocked`.                                                                        |
| Files Changed            | Every path the row touched, or `None`.                                                                  |
| Commands/Evidence        | Commands run and their pass/fail outcome, without raw secret or sensitive output.                       |
| Notes                    | Anything a reviewer needs that the other fields do not carry.                                           |

The four fields `Direct action`, `Source of truth`, `Exact applicable command`, and
`Acceptance criterion` are the ones P1-005 requires every expanded row to carry; they are declared
here so P1-005 has a schema to expand into rather than inventing one.

full. Two already exist in the working tree; the rest are declared before they are written so a
later drift check cannot mistake a known future file for an unexplained extra.

## Documentation Contract

The control contract every reader-facing edit in this program is measured against. Phase 2 records
it here so Phase 3 executes against one immutable revision rather than re-deriving intent per
document. Each subsection is written by the delivery item named in its heading.

### Source of Truth (P2-001)

Exactly one authority per fact class. A document that states a fact from any class must agree with
its authority or link to it; it may never carry a second, independently maintained copy.

| Fact class            | Sole authority                              | How a document may carry it                                | Verification                                                   |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Node and npm versions | the `volta` object in root `package.json`   | link, or show a command that reads the manifest            | `jq '.volta' package.json`                                     |
| Project inventory     | the resolved Nx workspace                   | name only projects that currently exist                    | `npm exec nx show projects -- --json`                          |
| Targets and ports     | that project's resolved Nx configuration    | package-manager-prefixed command plus its expected outcome | `npm exec nx show project <project> -- --json`                 |
| Product facts         | `roadmap.md` and the product specifications | summarize the purpose, link for the detail                 | cross-read the named canonical file                            |
| Behavior and design   | `specs/` plus focused reference documents   | link rather than restate the design                        | link resolution plus README-index validation                   |
| Contribution posture  | root policy plus `CONTRIBUTING.md`          | state closed external intake in consistent wording         | repository-wide phrase and link audit                          |
| Delivery mode         | the plans and trunk/worktree governance     | teach `worktree-to-pr` for authorized contributors         | link check plus workflow review                                |
| Repository relations  | the canonical ecosystem instructions        | distinguish content parity from `rhino-cli` byte identity  | relationship-text audit                                        |
| GitHub About metadata | the live GitHub repository fields           | the root README and the About panel must agree in intent   | `gh repo view --json description,homepageUrl,repositoryTopics` |
| Package description   | the Package Metadata Contract in `prd.md`   | package tooling and repository positioning must agree      | `jq -r '.description' package.json`                            |

Version pins are the sharpest case. A pin copied into prose drifts the moment the manifest moves,
which is exactly the defect the 2026-08-06 audit recorded and Phase 1 re-verified as still live in
nine documents. Prefer the link or the reading command; copy a pin only where the sentence genuinely
needs the literal number, and then only from the manifest.

### Voice and Reader Paths (P2-002)

The audit rubric. Every changed reader-facing document is read against all twelve clauses, and the
independent read-aloud pass at P3-012 and P7-004 uses this list verbatim.

| #   | Clause                                     | What a failure looks like                                                               |
| --- | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| V1  | Lead with the reader's purpose or problem  | An opening that begins "This directory contains…"                                       |
| V2  | Active voice, second person where natural  | "Configuration is performed by the developer" instead of "you configure"                |
| V3  | Explain niche terms on first use           | Nx, monorepo, Gherkin, BDD, or TDD used cold at an audience that does not know them     |
| V4  | Concrete verbs and outcomes                | "comprehensive", "robust", "seamless", "powerful"                                       |
| V5  | Short paragraphs, varied sentence openings | Every README stamped from one template with the same three opening moves                |
| V6  | Contractions where they sound natural      | Uniformly expanded forms that read stiff aloud                                          |
| V7  | Never minimize difficulty                  | "just", "simply", "obviously"                                                           |
| V8  | Outcome after the command                  | A command block with no statement of what the reader should see                         |
| V9  | Recovery after the likely failure          | A known failure mode named with no route out of it                                      |
| V10 | Emoji as wayfinding only, always labelled  | A bare emoji carrying meaning no text repeats                                           |
| V11 | READMEs stay maps                          | A long procedure inline that belongs in a tutorial, or facts that belong in a reference |
| V12 | End on a next step                         | A generic pile of links with no recommended move                                        |

**Shared opening.** The root README answers five questions in this order: what problem this
repository helps solve, who it is for, how it differs from its siblings, what its maturity and
contribution posture are, and which reader path to take. Sibling repositories appear here as
accurate one-line descriptions and links only — this program delivers no reader path, tutorial, or
metadata change for any of them.

**Reader paths.** Two, and a document that serves either must keep its order.

| Path                      | Ordered stages                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 🧭 Understand the product | mission → product and repository map → roadmap and specifications → next product document                                       |
| 🧰 Run OSE locally        | supported platform → prerequisites → clone and bootstrap → project discovery → visible first run → optional authorized workflow |

V4 and V5 are the two clauses this corpus fails most. Phase 1 found `comprehensive` live in 55
tracked documents, and the templated-opening pattern is what makes a 1,004-README corpus read as
machine-assembled even when every individual fact in it is correct.

### Supported Platforms (P2-003)

Three platform states, and every platform task in this program uses this wording contract. A
document may not promote a platform between states on its own authority.

| State                          | Platforms      | What a document may say                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------ | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Supported and verified         | macOS, Ubuntu  | Full prerequisites, bootstrap, and first-run instructions, each backed by a journey this program actually ran. |
| Possibly workable, unsupported | WSL2           | One short note: the Linux path may work under WSL2, but this program does not verify or support it.            |
| Not addressed                  | native Windows | Nothing. No instructions, no partial path, no "should also work" claim.                                        |

The WSL2 sentence is a fixed form, not a paraphrase target — "may work", "does not verify", "does
not support". A document that softens any of the three into a promise has changed the contract.

**Bootstrap order.** The 2026-08-06 audit recorded a circular prerequisite: `npm run doctor -- --fix`
runs through the Rust toolchain, so a clean machine cannot use it to install Rust when Cargo is
absent. Any document teaching bootstrap must state the minimum tools needed _before_ `npm install`
and doctor, derive versions from the manifest rather than restating them, give the expected output
after each command, and provide recovery for missing Cargo, Volta, Docker, and generated artifacts.
No document may offer an empty commit, a reset, a force push, a production apply, or a real-secret
step as onboarding verification.

### Contribution Posture (P2-004)

External contribution intake is closed. Authorized contributors deliver through `worktree-to-pr`.
Both halves must read consistently wherever contribution guidance appears — the root README,
`CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any document that routes a reader toward contributing.

| A document must                                                               | A document may not                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Describe external contributions as closed or authorization-only               | Invite pull requests, issues, or patches from the general public |
| Give authorized contributors the current `worktree-to-pr` workflow            | Teach or imply a direct-`main` workflow                          |
| State the delivery-boundary and PR expectations that actually apply           | Promise a response time, review turnaround, or triage commitment |
| Route a would-be external contributor somewhere useful instead of dead-ending | Leave "how to contribute" answered only by silence               |

No task in this program may introduce an invitation, a response-time promise, or a direct-`main`
workflow — not as an example, not as an aside, not in a template. Phase 1 re-verified the
2026-08-06 "contribution guidance contradicts policy" finding and confirmed it no longer reproduces:
`CONTRIBUTING.md` already states intake is closed and documents the internal worktree flow, and the
root README agrees. The contract's job here is to keep that true through the refresh, not to repair
it.

**The filename exemption.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` is uppercase, against the repository's lowercase
kebab-case filename rule, because GitHub only recognizes the file by that exact name. This is a
declared exemption, not drift. P3-005 verifies it is recorded as such; no task renames the file.

### Repository Metadata (P2-005)

The exact all-AI mutation contract. Phase 4 may apply only these values; it may not improvise
wording, add a topic, or reorder the set into a different meaning.

| Field       | Exact value                                                                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Description | `Open source platform for researching and building trustworthy, Sharia-compliant enterprise products.` |
| Homepage    | `https://oseplatform.com/`                                                                             |

Topics, as lowercase GitHub slugs, exactly ten:

`enterprise-software`, `erp`, `fsharp`, `islamic-finance`, `monorepo`, `nx`, `open-source`, `rust`,
`sharia-compliant`, `typescript`

The root `package.json` `description` field carries the same description string, byte for byte.

**Live state at this revision.** All four values already equal the contract: description matches
character for character, homepage matches, the live topic set is exactly these ten slugs, and
`jq -r '.description' package.json` returns the contract string. Phase 4 is therefore expected to
record verified equality rather than mutate anything, and P3-003A is a verification rather than an
edit. If a later read finds a difference, Phase 4 applies the contract value and reads it back for
exact equality; it does not negotiate.

**Procedure.** Capture the safe public fields before any mutation, apply through the repository's
authoritative command, read the same fields back, and compare for exact set equality. On failure,
restore the captured prior values. No captured field may include anything beyond the six approved
public ones.

### Safety Gates (P2-006)

Five gates. Every delivery unit in this program passes all five before it commits.

| Gate              | What it forbids                                                                                               | How it is discharged                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Read              | Reading a real `.env*` file at all                                                                            | Use `.env.example`, manifests, project configuration, safe tracked docs, and sanitized command output only. |
| Write             | Writing a secret value into any plan file, document, report, evidence file, commit message, or metadata field | Variable names and `<placeholder>` tokens only, never values.                                               |
| Staged diff       | Committing staged content that carries a credential or an environment file                                    | The deterministic staged gates, plus an independent AI sensitivity review of the staged diff.               |
| Identity boundary | Any staged change inside `apps/rhino-cli/` or `specs/apps/rhino/behavior/rhino-cli/`                          | `git diff --cached --name-only -- apps/rhino-cli specs/apps/rhino/behavior/rhino-cli` must return empty.    |
| Knowledge capture | Closing the plan with an untriaged or unsanitized learning                                                    | Every learning carries a generalization and a sensitivity verdict before archival.                          |

**On the identity boundary.** Two different rules overlap here, and conflating them would let this
plan claim protection it does not have.

The real byte-identity boundary is exactly seven pathspecs, read from `BOUNDARY_PATHS` in
`apps/rhino-cli/src/application/parity.rs`: `apps/rhino-cli/src`, `apps/rhino-cli/tests`,
`apps/rhino-cli/Cargo.toml`, `apps/rhino-cli/Cargo.lock`, `apps/rhino-cli/project.json`,
`apps/rhino-cli/LICENSE`, and `specs/apps/rhino/behavior/rhino-cli/gherkin`. Those are
byte-identical with the private sibling — zero carve-outs, not merely parallel content — and the
repository enforces it with the registered `rhino-cli parity manifest validate` gate on pre-push and
CI, against a 603-entry checksum manifest.

This plan's own no-edit scope is wider: nothing under `apps/rhino-cli/` or
`specs/apps/rhino/behavior/rhino-cli/` is edited at all. Two of the 27 paths classified
`identity-bound` — `apps/rhino-cli/README.md` and `specs/apps/rhino/behavior/rhino-cli/README.md` —
sit outside the checksum manifest and would not trip the parity gate. They are out of scope because
this plan says so, not because the manifest says so. Recording that honestly matters: a later reader
who believes the gate protects those two files would draw the wrong conclusion about what is safe to
change.

The staged check above is an earlier, cheaper tripwire than the parity gate, not a replacement: a
non-empty result stops the unit, and the change either moves to a separate cross-repository plan or
is reverted. It is deliberately scoped to the wider plan rule rather than the narrower manifest, so
it fires first. Describing the boundary in reader documentation is not editing it, so a document may
explain the relationship freely.

**On evidence.** No evidence file may contain a full environment dump, GitHub authentication state, a
remote URL with an embedded credential, a process environment, or a screenshot exposing browser or
session data. Every execution record in this program is sanitized at the point of writing rather than
scrubbed later, and no record carries an absolute local path, machine name, or account name.

## Reconciliation

_Populated by P1-007 and re-run by P7-001 and P9-003._

Every check below is machine-evaluated against the recorded revision
`028e8eed9e68112c49ccdee92d3cf29e70e6a4da`, not asserted by hand. Each has a non-zero floor or an
equality so an empty enumeration fails instead of passing (see `learnings.md` L-006).

| Check                                        | Expected | Actual        | Verdict |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------- | ------- |
| Tracked Markdown paths enumerated            | non-zero | 9,294         | PASS    |
| Enumerator cross-check agrees                | equal    | 9,294 = 9,294 | PASS    |
| Paths matched by exactly one rule            | all      | 9,294         | PASS    |
| Rule-coverage counts sum to the tree         | 9,294    | 9,294         | PASS    |
| Paths matched by no rule                     | 0        | 0             | PASS    |
| Paths with two terminal dispositions         | 0        | 0             | PASS    |
| Per-document rows equal the in-scope set     | 814      | 814           | PASS    |
| Duplicate row paths                          | 0        | 0             | PASS    |
| In-scope paths missing a row                 | 0        | 0             | PASS    |
| Row paths absent from the recorded tree      | 0        | 0             | PASS    |
| Unexplained extra paths                      | 0        | 0             | PASS    |
| Rows with a blank required field             | 0        | 0             | PASS    |
| Working-tree extras not declared planned-new | 0        | 0             | PASS    |
| `follow-up-required` states outstanding      | 0        | 0             | PASS    |

**Enumerators used.** Primary:
`git ls-tree -r --name-only 028e8eed9e68112c49ccdee92d3cf29e70e6a4da | grep -E '\.md$'`.
Independent cross-check:
`git diff --name-only 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904 028e8eed9e68112c49ccdee92d3cf29e70e6a4da -- '*.md'`
— a diff against git's empty-tree object, which enumerates the revision itself and, unlike
`git diff`'s cousin `git ls-files`, honours a glob pathspec. The two agree exactly at 9,294.

`git ls-files '*.md'` is deliberately **not** used as the cross-check. It has no revision-pinning
form: passing a SHA makes git read it as a pathspec and silently ignore it, so the command answers
about the index and working tree instead of the recorded revision. At this moment it returns 9,296,
because the two artifacts this plan creates are staged. A cross-check that drifts with the working
tree cannot re-run identically at P7-001 and P9-003, which is the whole point of recording it.

The working-tree extras check is a separate question and legitimately does read the working tree: it
compares `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` against the recorded tree and requires
every difference to appear in § Planned-New Paths.

**Interpretation.** The tree partitions cleanly: 9,294 tracked Markdown paths, each matched by
exactly one classification rule, 814 of them carrying an individual row and the remaining 8,480
carrying a rule-level bulk disposition with a matched count. No path is unclassified, doubly
classified, or silently dropped, and no path in the ledger fails to exist at the recorded revision.
Zero rows hold a non-terminal `follow-up-required` state, so nothing here blocks archival today;
P7-001 re-runs this table against the post-edit tree and P9-003 re-runs it at archival.

### P9-003 Re-Run at Archival

Re-run on 2026-08-21 against the **staged post-archival index**, tree
`4e8dd974b19adb03452cb4983bc9e4ea61958761`, with `origin/main` at `7ebf8fec3`. Two independent
enumerators were used, as in the runs above: `git ls-files` reading the index directly, and
`git ls-tree -r` against the written tree object.

| Check                             | Expected | Actual        | Verdict |
| --------------------------------- | -------- | ------------- | ------- |
| Tracked Markdown paths enumerated | non-zero | 9,301         | PASS    |
| Enumerator cross-check agrees     | equal    | 9,301 = 9,301 | PASS    |
| Paths added over `7ebf8fec3`      | 12       | 12            | PASS    |
| Paths removed over `7ebf8fec3`    | 10       | 10            | PASS    |
| Net change                        | +2       | +2            | PASS    |
| Added paths accounted for         | all      | 12 of 12      | PASS    |
| Per-document rows                 | 814      | 814           | PASS    |
| Duplicate row paths               | 0        | 0             | PASS    |
| Rows absent from the staged tree  | 0        | 0             | PASS    |

**Interpretation.** The archival move is not additive and the arithmetic says so: ten Markdown paths
left `plans/in-progress/repository-onboarding-readme-refresh/` and twelve appeared under
`plans/done/2026-08-21__repository-onboarding-readme-refresh/`. Ten of the twelve are the same
documents at their new path; the other two are `artifacts/execution-record-closeout.md` and
`evidence/README.md`, both declared in § Planned-New Paths before they were written. Nothing is
unexplained in either direction.

The "0 rows absent from the staged tree" result is the one worth guarding, because a path-rewriting
move is exactly the operation that would strand a row. The detector was proven by appending a
deliberately nonexistent path to the row list and confirming it reported 1 absent — so the zero is a
measurement, not a silent no-op.
